_note: Frames LIVE data from the mlops hub. The frontend fetches https://monishkamwal.github.io/mlops/api-metrics.json and fills the series. First real capture published 2026-10-20 (EKS run 39511787204). Contract shape: { captured_at, window:{start,end,step_seconds,minutes}, queries:{ <key>:{ promql, unit, series:[{labels, points:[[unix_ts, value], ...]}] } } }. Each `section.contractKeys` names the queries that section renders. Units: latency=seconds, rps=reqps, error_rate=ratio, node_*=ratio. An empty `series` array is a real result (e.g. error_rate_5xx empty = no 5xx). The page header date comes from `captured_at`.
title: Performance
subtitle: A snapshot from the last EKS dress rehearsal
intro_md:
Once a month the platform builds a real Kubernetes cluster, load-tests the *same* container image that serves the live demo, captures these numbers straight from Prometheus — then tears everything down.

A deliberate snapshot, not a live feed: nothing is left running, because nothing needs to be. What you see below is the real capture from the last run.

sections.title: Response time under load
sections.body: How long the model takes to answer while traffic is pouring in, shown as a spread from typical (p50) to worst-case (p99). The p99 is the honest number — it's what the slowest one-in-a-hundred request waits. Even flat out, typical responses land in a few hundredths of a second.

sections.title: Throughput
sections.body: How many requests a second the service handled during the test, and how that held up as the load climbed and settled. This is a stress test, not everyday demo traffic — the point is to find a sustained ceiling, and nearly all of it is the /predict path doing the real work.

sections.title: Errors under load
sections.body: The share of requests that failed with a server error while under load. The cleanest result is the one you can't draw — an empty line.

emptyState.label: no errors
emptyState.text: No server errors during the test. The series is empty because nothing failed — the model served every request the load test threw at it.

sections.title: Cluster headroom
sections.body: How hard the three cluster nodes were actually working — processor and memory use across the run. It shows whether the load test pushed the machines to their limit or left room to spare.

footer: These series are the real Prometheus capture from the last monthly load test, served straight from api-metrics.json — no screenshots, no hand-typed numbers.
